**Weights count situations (P117, 16 October 2026).** Of section 140's two AI readings (“at a parting the branch is settled only when taken, the form the open future takes in identification”; “reading weights as chances adds the premise that the course which happens is typical”), Ren wrote: “i mean we are describing what everything obeys, but at every moment, the actual change depends on the situation … just saying we are all one doesn't make it true, the situation makes it true”, and asked what to do with this for the second ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-16-the-situation-makes-it-true.md)). Section 144 adds one core module, `Becoming.Situations` (13 theorems, no axiom, no premise beyond what each law names), on Weighted's and Typicality's definitions.
- **With the situation as the move, the law is determined.** A step weighing k is taken in k situations; the law whose moves are the situations is determined and takes exactly the steps of positive weight (`finerLaw_determined`, `finerLaw_step_iff`). A law whose steps are those of positive weight is this law with the situation forgotten.
- **Natural weights count situations.** For every process with listed moves and configurations and natural weights of steps, summing any reading of the courses over the finer courses of n steps is summing it over the courses, each times its weight (`sum_finer`), so the finer courses number the sum over histories (`finer_count`).
- **The law of large numbers counts situations.** On two values with p and q situations a step there are (p + q)ⁿ finer courses, a course is taken by its weight of them (`situations_of_course`, each course occurring once, `total_only`), and those whose course deviates by at least d number, times d, at most n·p·q·(p + q)ⁿ (`situations_typical`). Which situation happens is not a count.
- **Readings (the AI's reading of Ren's words, taken by Ren the same day, below).** The core states what every situation obeys; the situation makes the actual change true; a branching law is a determined law with the situation forgotten; a chance is a number of situations of a kind, so stating it needs no premise of typicality, while foretelling the course needs its situation. These replace section 140's two readings, whose text stays as history.
- **Ren's judgment.** On 16 October, answering the report of this section's results, which restated these readings, Ren wrote “yes, i take those readings”. The four readings above are therefore Ren's; the three notes on Ren's words remain the AI's notes. Whether, with a bound, a class's name reads as its finite future is still for Ren.
- **Notes on Ren's words (the AI's).** The law of gravitation is shared by all planets; the value of gravity on each is situational, so the example holds of the value. Representing the actual change as fixed by a situation needs no axiom, but where weights cancel or readings depend on context (`Interference.cancels`, `Becoming.Context`, `Becoming.Quantum`, P112 in progress), the situation must include the context of the reading: counts of context-free situations do not give those statistics. “Just saying we are all one doesn't make it true” agrees with the nondual method: oneness is a requirement of method, and particular truths come from the situation.
- **Boundaries.** Natural weights only; counting per course and the law of large numbers for two values only (per course for every process needs listings without repetition); which situation is actual is not derived. Scratch build on main 6c62e13e: empty axiom reports. Not yet independently reviewed.

**What a finite history refutes, integration I4b item 3 (16 October 2026).** Ren chose “Closest gaps first” on the I4 classification table ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-16-i4-decisions.md)). The table read PrefixSafety as a join candidate. On infinite traces, a finitely refutable property holds within its prefix closure, and the prefix closure is the least finitely refutable superset. Recurrence and eventual truth are not finitely refutable, and properties given by prefix tests are. Becoming.Horizon stated what no finite prefix decides, but not what a finite history refutes (section 139). This section states it for every process, with PrefixSafety's prefix topology as the instance of the process of all sequences. IdealWarrant generalizes the same form to posets; it belongs to the general mathematical line Ren left outside the spine for now.
- **Agreement, refutability, adherence** (`Becoming.Horizon`, no premise; 12 → 34 theorems).
  - Agreement up to a horizon is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, and holds at every smaller horizon (`Run.AgreeUpTo.refl`, `symm`, `trans`, `mono`).
  - A reading is refutable where every run outside it has a horizon within which every agreeing run is outside (`Refutable`); verifiable dually (`Verifiable`).
  - A run adheres to a reading where at every horizon it agrees with a run inside (`Adheres`). Runs inside adhere, adherence grows with the reading, and adhering to the adherent is adhering.
- **A refutable reading holds where a run adheres, up to double negation** (`Refutable.not_not`). A refutable superset so holds at every run adhering to the subset (`Refutable.adheres_least`), the core form of the closure being least. For a stable reading, adhering is holding (`Refutable.adheres_iff`).
- **Witnesses.**
  - A run adhering to a reading while outside it shows the reading is not refutable (`not_refutable_of_adheres`), and dually not verifiable (`not_verifiable_of_adheres`).
  - In the process whose runs are all sequences (`Sequences.process`), splicing a constant after a horizon keeps agreement within it. So recurrence and eventual occurrence are not refutable, and never occurring is not verifiable (`Sequences.recurs_not_refutable`, `eventually_not_refutable`, `never_not_verifiable`).
- **Readings made of tests.**
  - The test at n is Boolean and fixed by the history through step n + 1 (`ByPrefixes`), and the reading is that no test fails (`Passes`).
  - It holds at every run adhering to it, with no double negation, since the tests are decided (`adheres_passes`).
  - Given Markov's principle, that a Boolean sequence not all false has a true term (`Markov`), it is refutable (`refutable_passes`).
- **Boundary.** Asked of every process, refutability of every reading made of tests is exactly Markov's principle (`refutable_passes_iff_markov`).
  - The witness is the process of all Boolean sequences, with the test at n reading term n.
  - A refuting horizon for a sequence not all false either shows a true term or, spliced to all false after it, gives an agreeing run passing every test.
  - What a refuting history must find is a failed test where it is only known that not all pass. PrefixSafety's `boundary_closed` takes this step implicitly, by classical reasoning.
- **PrefixSafety** (`PrefixSafetyCorrespondence`, periphery, with its own checker).
  - Correspondences: `SamePrefix` is `Run.AgreeUpTo` on the runs of the sequences; finite refutability is `Refutable`; and the prefix closure is adherence. Recurrence and the termination event are not finitely refutable by the core's `Sequences` laws. These five have empty axiom reports.
  - With classical reasoning: holding within the closure, the closure being least, and `boundary_closed` follow from `Refutable.not_not`, `adheres_least`, `Markov` and `refutable_passes`. These four use standard axioms only.
  - PrefixSafety's statements and its package receipt are unchanged.
- **Checker.** PrefixSafety lies outside the Lean root the core indexes. `check_prefix_safety_correspondence.py` is generated by `make_checker.py` and then patched by `make_prefix_checker.py`:
  - the Lean root points to `generative-basis/lean`;
  - PrefixSafety and the instance are indexed from the completion package;
  - PrefixSafety matches the package receipt, which `check.py` writes only after a fresh compile with every audit passing.
  - A dry run under Lean 4.30.0-rc2 passed, with its receipt written to a scratch folder: 9 theorems, five of them with empty reports. Only the new Becoming.Horizon lacked a receipt, pending the core run.
- **Decidability inventory.** `refutable_passes_iff_markov` joins the boundary theorems, and the boundary sentence gains the gate origin and prefix refutation. Proof-only theorems are unchanged (224).
- **Records.** The new record what-a-finite-history-refutes reuses becoming-finite-horizon's `Run.AgreeUpTo`. becoming-finite-horizon and no-finite-part-bears-taking are rebound, their claims unchanged.
- **Not stated.**
  - Whether `Renewable`'s renewing class is refutable: the two runs of `prefix_does_not_decide` vary with the horizon, so no fixed run adheres to the other class.
  - That stability is exactly what removing the double negation needs.
  - IdealWarrant's poset form, and the converse of `refutable_passes`.
- **Boundary and reading.** The law says what refutability gives, not which actual readings are refutable; that depends on the process. PrefixSafety's traces are functions on the natural numbers, not a model of an actual history. The reading, which is the AI's and pending Ren: what a finite record can show is that a run lies outside a refutable reading; that it lies inside is only not refuted.
- **Next in I4b.**
  - Lasting: König lifting (FiniteBranching).
  - Selection: PluralRecords and TieBreaking, after P110 lands.

**Lifting where branching is finite, integration I4b item 4 (16 October 2026).** Ren chose “Closest gaps first” on the I4 classification table ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-16-i4-decisions.md)). The table read FiniteBranching as a join candidate: for a finitely branching relation, finite paths of every length from a node give an infinite path (König lifting). Becoming.Lasting stated that every admissible course stays (`Lasts`; what no course leaves is what lasts every horizon, `kernel_iff_lasts`), but not that some course goes on (section 139). This section states it for every process and says what each step needs.
- **Lasting some course** (`Becoming.Lasting`, no premise; 69 → 89 theorems; Lasting now imports Becoming.Likeness).
  - `Continues P n s`: some course of n steps starts at s. `Unbounded P s`: courses of every length do. `FinitelyBranching`: the successors of each configuration are listed.
  - Where the process branches finitely, the depth reached is decided (`Continues.decided`), level by level through the listed successors, with no decision of equality.
- **An unbounded successor, up to double negation** (`Unbounded.step_not_not`). Where each step of a decided decreasing family is met by some member of a list, some member meets every step, up to double negation (`list_throughout_not_not`). The goal is a refutation, so whether the first member fails somewhere may be taken as decided.
- **Given `EitherThroughout`**, an unbounded configuration has an unbounded successor (`Unbounded.step_of_either`), and of finitely many starts one is unbounded (`unbounded_start_of_either`). Both are Likeness's `EitherThroughout.list` on the listed successors or starts.
- **A run from a selection.** A selection of a step staying in a family gives a run from each member (`runOf`). So `EitherThroughout` and a choice of an unbounded successor lift courses of every length to a run along unbounded configurations (`lifting`).
- **Boundary.** Asked of every finitely branching process, an unbounded successor is exactly `EitherThroughout` (`step_iff_either`).
  - The witness is Likeness's `Chains`: with two decided decreasing families, one holding at each step, the fork `two` is unbounded (`TwoChains.two_unbounded`).
  - An unbounded successor is a chain start whose family holds throughout (`TwoChains.side_of_unbounded`).
- **Without finite branching: the fan.** A root stepping to an arm of every length has courses of every length (`Fan.root_unbounded`), but the arm of length n has no course of n + 1 steps, so no successor is unbounded (`Fan.no_unbounded_step`). Finite branching is what lifting needs, not only what the proof uses.
- **FiniteBranching** (`FiniteBranchingCorrespondence`, periphery, with its own checker).
  - Correspondences: a relation is the process with one move; `Reach` is `Continues` and `Unbounded` is `Unbounded`; and listed children make the process finitely branching. These four have empty axiom reports.
  - Classical reasoning gives `EitherThroughout`, and Lean's choice selects an unbounded successor. `finite_unbounded`, `unbounded_child` and the three liftings then follow from the core laws, each `_by_core`, with standard axioms only.
  - FiniteBranching's statements and its package receipt are unchanged.
- **Checker.** It follows the PrefixSafety pattern. `make_prefix_checker.py` now takes `SPEC MODULE`; with no arguments it reproduces the PrefixSafety checker byte for byte.
  - A dry run under Lean 4.30.0-rc2 passed: 9 theorems and 10 declarations, four of them with empty reports. Only the new Becoming.Lasting lacked a receipt.
  - FiniteBranching is bound through the instance receipt, as fixed at the I4b-3 landing.
- **Decidability inventory.**
  - Proof-only theorems go 224 → 226: `list_throughout_not_not` splits, and `TwoChains.branching` builds a list.
  - Theorems proving decidedness go 136 → 137 (`Continues.decided`).
  - `Lasting.step_iff_either` joins the boundary theorems.
- **Records.** The new record lifting-where-branching-is-finite reuses tests-fix-likeness-where-determined's `EitherThroughout` and `Chains`. Three market records citing Lasting are rebound, their claims unchanged.
- **Author counterreview.**
  - The core separates the two classical steps of the periphery proof: `Classical.not_forall` is exactly `EitherThroughout`, and `Classical.choose` is a selection.
  - Importing Likeness grows Lasting's closure from 5 to 31 modules. The five modules depending on Lasting rebuild with empty reports.
  - Not proved: a run without a selection (the boundary of dependent choice, next to but distinct from Keeping's `plans_iff_choice`).
- **Boundary and reading.** Lifting gives a run's existence, not an effective selection or a physical infinity. The reading, which is the AI's and pending Ren: courses of every length are not yet one course going on; where branching is finite, what lies between them is exactly knowing which of two branches goes on throughout.
- **Next in I4b.** Selection: PluralRecords and TieBreaking, after P110 lands.

**Readings decided on Ren's delegation (P110, 16 October 2026).** After P107 landed Ren asked, “What's the best choices to make? please make best of your judgement, and push the frontier of completeness” ([words](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-15-delegated-choices.md)). Section 147 reads this as a delegation: the readings and names that the theory's §8, CONTINUATION-GROUNDING-PLAN §6 and the records left to Ren are decided by the AI, each with its reasons and what would change it, and recorded as the AI's decisions on the delegation, not as Ren's own; Ren can reverse any of them. [DELEGATED-CHOICES](../../DELEGATED-CHOICES.md) holds D1–D39. They change no theorem and add no premise; the theorems of declined readings stay. Some are decided by checked results rather than judgement: the activity reading of generative and degenerative is declined because arising and ceasing recurring coincide in finite worlds (D2); registration is read formally as the law's sensitivity, the least registration it reads through (D37). D34 first adopted “situationally means the bound”; Ren's reply, “not sure what's the reading 1, but reality is always situational”, now decides it. P116's readings, posed after that reply, were left to Ren, and on 16 October Ren took the AI's reading of their clarification (section 144). With a bound, a class's name reads as its finite future: D34 had adopted it as an analogy for a precise form of 名可名, and on 16 October Ren took the same reading (“take 2”, [words](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-16-finite-name-and-open-proofs.md)), the theorem being that within a bound kinds have finite names and 名可名 an analogy only, so Ren's words decide it and answer section 144's “still for Ren”. D39 decides P115's readings, which its owner left to Ren or this delegation: the coupling strength is read formally as how strongly a formation registers (识 itself stays Ren's), and in Ren's “highly entangled system” entanglement reads as coupling strength, as Ren's own sentence glosses it, not as quantum entanglement. Not within the delegation: Ren's own texts and terms, Ren's testimony on the invariance step, warrant, I4, the representation decisions Ren reserved and decisions of review. 101 records gain one paired, dated note each; the Lean docstrings of 51 modules and the root, and the Lean README, fold the decisions, comments only, with the code outside comments asserted unchanged. Earlier sections' “pending Ren” are read through the records' decisions; their text stays as evidence. Not yet independently reviewed.

**Where novelty's gain comes from (P111, 16 October 2026).** Under the same delegation, section 148 adds `Becoming.Gain` (30 theorems, no axiom). With the rest of the whole counted as a relatum (section 85), every rise is given, with no premise: across a step at which a family's stock rises, some relatum gives it more than it takes, a formation taking part or the rest, found by checking each one taking part (`Flow.rise_netGiver`, `Flow.rise_given`). Under the first law a family without repetition that rises is given net by the rest or is open there (`Flow.rise_from_rest_or_open`). A finite whole has no boundary to cross, so every rise of it is the rest's, and with the rest idle it stays within its stock, returns and forgets, and is not new at every step (`Flow.whole_not_new_of_rest_idle`): unceasing generation within a bounded whole is return. Novelty needs gain, along consecutive steps or first visits (`Web.rises_late_of_firsts`), and so does endless new formation where what forms requires a fixed amount within the family, since a step at which something is first supported is a first visit (`Web.newAt_of_first`); under the first law each such rise comes from the rest or across the boundary, for every family without repetition holding it (`Flow.new_beyond_every`). Counting on is given each unit by the rest (`Flow.counting_given_by_rest`). Readings (D5, D7): gain from beyond the part reads as these two ways in, and a finite whole new without end is one whose listing leaves out what gives to it. Known: conservation and the pigeonhole principle; the increment is the statement with no premise and the two ways in. Not stated: whether the bound by the configurations within the stock is reached, and the exact ratio of gain to novelty. Not yet independently reviewed.

**When readings in context glue, for parity (P112, 16 October 2026).** Section 149 adds `Becoming.Gluing` (81 theorems, no axiom), the next step of contextual-registration (section 96), “the general parity obstruction; probabilistic contextuality”. For claims constrained by parity in each context, a contradiction is a selection of contexts, repetition allowed, counting every claim an even number of times while the parities it requires add up to odd. Every context-free assignment fails an odd number of its contexts (`ParitySystem.unmet_odd`); with equality of claims decided and the claims listed without repetition this is the only obstruction, found by elimination as in linear equations over two values (`ParitySystem.global_or_contradicts`, `ParitySystem.glues_iff`). A mixture of context-free assignments meets at most m − 1 of a contradiction's m contexts on average, and readings indexed by context meet all m (`ParitySystem.mixture_le`, `ParitySystem.indexed_met`): Specker's boxes (2 of 3), the CHSH game (3 of 4, the classical bound) and the Mermin–Peres square (5 of 6) are instances, and section 96's `Specker.noGlobal` and `Square.noGlobal` follow from their certificates. A cycle of claims related as equal or different is met by a context-free assignment exactly where its differ relations are even in number (`Cycle.met_iff_even`): the periphery's `CorrectionRelations.cycle_compatible_iff_even` in core form, as the I4b row leaves it with P112; the correspondence theorem between the two is not written. Reading (D33): the difference between m − 1 and m is what the context carries; a value is a registration in context, a relation. Known: the parity proofs of Kochen–Specker (Mermin, Peres), CHSH (1969), Abramsky and Hardy's logical Bell inequalities (2012) and the alternative for linear equations over two values; the increment is the exact law with no axiom, in the core, with its instances. Not stated: the quantum values (Tsirelson's bound needs real amplitudes) and contextuality beyond parity. Not yet independently reviewed.

**The open proofs of parting and counting (P119, 16 October 2026).** After the AI explained the finite-name reading, Ren wrote: “take 2, and do the open proofs” ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-16-finite-name-and-open-proofs.md)). P110 records option 2, the finite name as an analogy. Section 150 proves what sections 140 and 144 left open, with no axiom and no premise beyond what each law names; existing declarations do not change.
- **Parting** (18 → 43 theorems; it now imports `Becoming.Lasting`).
  - Where runs part only before step T, the learner by the least bound is right from 2(T + N) − 1 on (`late_right`).
  - For a process with listed moves and configurations and decided steps and registered values, the learner given the world (`worldLearner`) is right at a step on every run exactly where no two runs part there (`world_right_iff`, `some_right_iff`). It is built from the prelude alone: where a list of N holds every configuration, a course of N steps (`Lasting.Continues`) gives courses of every length, with no decidability and no selection (`unbounded_of_continues`), where Lasting's lifting for finite branching holds up to double negation.
- **Typicality** (32 → 43). Concentration is exponential, the counting form of Chernoff's bound (`concentrated`, `few_far_ahead`).
- **Situations** (13 → 38).
  - Through an event, any number of values counts as two (`sum_event`), so the law of large numbers and exponential concentration count situations for every event.
  - For every process, a course is taken by its weight of situations times how often it is listed (`situations_take`, `situations_of_course_listed`).
  - In any weights, steps weighing the sum over their situations are counted by them (`sum_finer_weights`).
  - A signed weight is a pair of counts of situations, those composing to adding and those to subtracting (`signed_counts`). Where signed weights cancel, the situations do not (`cancels_situations`).
- **Still open.** Real or complex amplitudes, infinite or undecided processes for the converse, and the exactness of 2(T + N) − 1.

**Selection by the record alone, integration I4b item 2 (16 October 2026).** (Reframed the same day in section 153 at Ren's correction, as selection through a model of the options, its reading withdrawn; the text below is kept as evidence.) Ren chose “Closest gaps first” on the I4 classification table ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-16-i4-decisions.md)). The table read PluralRecords and TieBreaking as join candidates: a rule treating the centers alike (exchanging two centers' entries exchanges its output) can serve center k exactly when no other center's entry equals k's (`servable_iff_untied`), and a lottery treating them alike gives tied centers equal weight (`tied_equal_weight`). Becoming.Selection stated that selection through registration reaches exactly what registers (`Web.selects_alike_iff`), not selection by the record alone (section 139). This section states it for any options and entries of any kind. The names follow Ren's rule of the same day for joined modules ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-16-joined-module-names.md), board rule 8): the core law, the instance module and the record's title use the core's structural vocabulary, and the instance module is named after the core law.
- **Reading the record alone** (`Becoming.Selection`, namespace `Relabel`, no premise; 43 → 67 theorems, no new import).
  - Options are told apart only by what a record holds of each. Exchanging two options (`Relabel.swap`) is an involution.
  - A selection reads the record alone (`Relabel.Equivariant`) when exchanging two options' entries exchanges what it selects; likewise a valuation (`EquivariantValue`) and a choice of at most one option (`EquivariantChoice`). Exchanging two tied options leaves the record as it was (`fixed_of_tied`).
- **It parts exactly what the record parts.** Tied options are selected alike (`Equivariant.tied`), and two options are selected alike by every selection reading the record alone exactly when the record ties them (`selected_alike_iff`). The witness selects the options whose entry equals a given value. This is the form of `Web.selects_alike_iff`.
- **Singling out.** A selection reading the record alone that selects at most one option selects no tied option (`Equivariant.untied`), and none at a full tie of two or more (`Equivariant.none_of_full_tie`). Holding an entry alone (`Alone`) is such a selection (`alone_equivariant`, `alone_single`), so an option can be singled out exactly when no other option's entry ties it (`singled_iff_untied`). Both directions are stated as relations, with no search.
- **Values and choices.**
  - A valuation reading the record alone, such as a weight on each option, gives tied options equal values, and every option the same at a full tie (`EquivariantValue.tied`, `full_tie`). The options taking a value form a selection reading the record alone (`level`); a constant valuation reads it (`const`); two options are valued alike by every such valuation exactly when tied (`valued_alike_iff`).
  - The option a choice reading the record alone chooses is a selection reading it (`EquivariantChoice.selects`), so the choice chooses no tied option and withholds at a full tie (`untied`, `withholds_of_full_tie`).
- **PluralRecords and TieBreaking** (`SelectionRelabelCorrespondence`, periphery, with its own checker).
  - Correspondences: a record is the core's record of entries over `Fin n`; exchanging two centers is `Relabel.swap` (`transpose_eq_swap`); a rule treating the centers alike is a choice reading the record alone (`treatsAlike_iff`); a lottery treating them alike has weights reading the record alone and an unchanged withholding weight (`lotteryAlike_iff`); and holding an entry alone is `Relabel.Alone` (`alone_iff`).
  - The core laws give `tied_not_served`, `all_tied_forces_withholding`, `servable_iff_untied`, `tied_equal_weight`, `full_tie_equal_weights`, `uniform_alike` and `point_mass_not_alike_at_tie`, each `_by_core`. For the converse of `servable_iff_untied` the core gives holding alone its invariance and uniqueness, and `PluralRecords.pick` finds the holder in `Fin n`.
  - All 13 theorems have empty axiom reports. The originals' definitions and statements are unchanged.
- **Checker.** `make_relabel_checker.py` generates `check_selection_relabel_correspondence.py` from `../integration-i3e/make_checker.py relabel.json` and makes four changes:
  - the Lean root;
  - the two originals and the instance are added to the module index;
  - the originals are checked here, since they import only Lean's prelude and have no machine receipt (their build record is `inquiry-warrant/BUILD.md`): every declaration is audited with the instance's and must have an empty report;
  - the originals name declarations with `?` and `'`, so they are scanned with those characters admitted, and audit lines are read anchored at their start, so a primed name is read whole.
  - TieBreaking prints one warning, the unused hypothesis `noWithhold` of `full_tie_open_uniform`, kept as stated. It is the only output allowed, and the receipt records it.
  - A dry run under Lean 4.30.0-rc2 passed, with its receipt in a scratch folder: 13 theorems and 72 declaration audits, all empty. The only missing receipt was the new Becoming.Selection, which awaits its core run.
- **Decidability inventory.** Relabel's four definitions are classified as exchanging two values. Statement-level uses go 387 → 409, the 22 laws naming the options' decided equality. Proof-only theorems go 233 → 234 with `Relabel.alone_single`, which tells whether two options are the same.
- **Records.** The new record selection-by-the-record-alone (F04) is related to selection-through-registration. Three records citing Selection.lean are rebound, their claims unchanged.
- **Author counterreview.**
  - The law is new to the spine: Selection had only the registration form. The core states it more generally than the originals: any options with decided equality, entries of any kind, as relations with no search over listed options. The originals' converse searches `Fin n` with `pick`; that step stays in the periphery.
  - Exchanging two options tells whether the input is either of them, so `DecidableEq` is a condition each statement names (classified like Learning's `swapTo`). Stating the law for arbitrary permutations rather than transpositions would remove the need from the definition, but "tied options are selected alike" still needs the transposition to exist.
  - Names follow board rule 8: the originals' `TreatsAlike`, `LotteryAlike` and `servable` are not carried into the core, which uses `Relabel`, `Equivariant`, `Alone` and `singled_iff_untied`; the instance module is named after the core law. The `_by_core` theorems keep the original theorems' names to show what they restate.
  - Not proved: that an option singled out is found by a choice function (a search); the same law over records of pairwise relations.
- **Boundary and reading.** The core law says what a selection reading the record alone can part, not which selection should be used. Whether an equal chance legitimately breaks a tie, and priority by size or by turn, keep the originals' scope ([TIE-BREAKING-LEGITIMACY](../../../history/root-foundation/TIE-BREAKING-LEGITIMACY.md)). The reading, which is the AI's and pending Ren: which option is which is not among the record's relations; to part what the record ties takes a further recorded relation, such as an order of arrival or an agreement, as the gap of selection through registration closes only through relations.
- **Next in I4b.** The four items are complete: Gated, Selection, Horizon and Lasting. IdealWarrant waits for Ren to place it; when joined it takes a structural name under rule 8.

**How a carried difference grows (P118, 16 October 2026).** P115's record how-much-difference-arrives listed a general theory of loops, the strength around a loop and its runaway, first in its next steps, as `Becoming.Propagation` listed it among what is not derived; comparison-where-the-rest-responds and runaway-distance-unregistered (P55) asked to define a loop in general and state a runaway as a theorem, and the chapter's §8 lists the general theory of loops under feedback and reach. On 12 October Ren compared the theory with quantum dynamics and "Fermi's diagrams": “there are so many patterns and loops but we can still find a way to to integrate so we can still calculate this effects but how how accurate can we do that uh what is the limitation do we have losses”, with the goal “move towards 100%” ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-12-move-towards-100.md)). Section 152 adds one core module, `Becoming.Loops` (113 theorems, no axiom, no premise beyond the strengths each theorem names), on Propagation's carried amount.
- **Orders.** Order j (`carriedWithin`) is what routes of at most j responses carry, each order being what the strengths make of the order below (`carriedFrom`); the orders rise to the carried amount, and order j is exact up to step j (`carriedWithin_exact`).
- **No loop upstream, a finite order is exact.** Couplings (`Couples`), chains (`Coupled`), loops (`OnLoop`) and upstream (`Upstream`) are defined on the positive strengths. Where no chain of j + 1 couplings ends at c, order j is exact there; with every condition listed a chain as long as the list passes a loop (`loop_of_coupledInto`, pigeonhole by `revisits_within`), so where no loop lies upstream the order one less than the number of conditions is exact at every step (`carriedWithin_exact_of_no_loop`).
- **A loop upstream, every order misses.** Where the couplings hold at every step, the order missed rises by one per coupling and by the loop's length every time around, so a fed loop upstream leaves every order inexact (`carriedWithin_lt_of_loop`), and a finite order is exact from every start exactly where no loop lies upstream (`finite_order_iff_no_loop`); the couplings must hold at every step, as a loop coupled at the first step only leaves order one exact (`Loops.Once.not_always`).
- **The strength around a loop.** Along a chain, what reaches its start arrives times the product of the strengths (`carried_along`); around a loop it returns multiplied, every time around, by at least one plus the product of the strengths (`carried_around`, `carried_runaway`), the one from levels holding what they are given.
- **Accuracy of a cut.** With the part giving no gap after the start, starting gaps at most D and the strengths into each condition at most M a step, order j carries at most D times the sum over i ≤ j of C(t, i)·M^i (`carriedWithin_le_withinBound`, `Loops.withinBound_eq`), the carried amount at most D(1 + M)^t (`carried_le_geomBound`), and a cut at order j misses at most the rest of that sum (`carried_le_carriedWithin_add`); a self-loop attains all three (`Loops.SelfLoop.attained`).
- **Polynomial exactly where no loop lies upstream.** Where no loop lies upstream the carried amount is at most a polynomial of degree one less than the number of conditions (`carried_le_polynomial`). With the same formations and strengths at every step (`stationary`), every loop at least doubles what reaches it every time around (`carried_doubles_around`, `carried_doubles_into`), and a doubling outgrows every polynomial (`Loops.not_poly_of_doubling`), so a polynomial bound holds exactly where no loop lies upstream (`polynomial_iff_no_loop`); by `most_difference_arrives` the same holds of the most difference that can arrive for every law with those strengths (`gap_polynomial_iff_no_loop`, with `most_difference_within` and `gap_le_polynomial` where no loop lies upstream).
- **Readings (the AI's, pending Ren).** The orders are the integration Ren asked about, like a sum over diagrams by their number of vertices (the AI reads "Fermi's diagrams" as Feynman diagrams), `Loops.binom` counting the time orderings of the responses; the accuracy of a cut is the rest of the sum, attained; where no loop lies upstream a finite order loses nothing, and where one does every finite order loses something. `Becoming.Weighted` (P82) answered the same question for sums over histories. Only a loop makes a difference run away: P115's chain grows linearly and its self-loop doubles, the two ends of this law. Which loops a world has is its situation (Ren, 16 October, “the situation makes it true”).
- **Ren's decisions (16 October).** Ren decided the three readings ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-16-loops-readings-and-delegated-choices.md)). The first is taken in the AI's wording: Ren meant Feynman diagrams, the match structural, not physical; the integration Ren asked about, for laws that are not determined, is P82's sum over histories with its four losses, and P118's orders are the same structural kind, organized by number of responses as Feynman diagrams are by vertices; the two are not yet joined, which is a further proof. The second is right with its qualifiers: running away means faster than every polynomial, of the most difference that can arrive, not of every law, and couplings that hold only at some steps are open; in one sentence, the most difference that can arrive grows faster than every polynomial only through a loop, and through every loop that couples at every step. The third is taken in a refined form for now: which loops a world has is part of its situation, loops forming and dissolving within the unfolding and the theorems taking them as they stand at each step, open to revision once a loop-formation theorem exists (Ren: “leave it pending until a loop-formation theorem exists”).
- **Boundaries.** The strengths are supplied; the equivalences need couplings at every step, stated for the same formations and strengths at every step; couplings that come and go, how fast a runaway is beyond the product of the strengths, real strengths and amounts, continuous time and infinitely many conditions are open; the runaway is of the most difference that can arrive, attained by the carrying law, not of every law. The mathematics is standard (Picard iteration of a linear comparison system, nilpotent on an acyclic coupling graph); what is new is its statement on the core's laws with no premise, the attained accuracy, and the equivalence for every law. **Selection through a model of the options, a reframing of section 151 (I4b item 2 follow-up, 16 October 2026).** Having read section 151's result, Ren wrote: “selection's “record-only” doesn't seem right - it is about the cognitive model, not just record, which feels as long as we remember all pasts we can move forward without wisdom”. After the AI's investigation and recommendations Ren wrote “go ahead with the reframing, first title, keep names, (a)” ([words](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-16-selection-through-a-model.md)). Section 153 reframes section 151's result accordingly. No Lean statement changes; one link to `Becoming.Learning`'s lumping is added, and the earlier reading is withdrawn.
- **Why reframe.**
  - In the core, “record” means the kept past. Section 151's title “Selection by the record alone” and its reading, “to part what the record ties takes a further recorded relation, such as an order of arrival or an agreement”, suggested that remembering more is enough.
  - That is wrong on both counts. Perfect memory cannot separate options whose histories are alike. Where memory does separate them, as by who came first, the law says nothing about whether that difference matters.
  - The entries section 151 reads are the selector's model of the options: what it can tell apart. In the core a model is a lumping (`Learning.Lumped`; 理, on Ren's reading, is the modeling of the laws of structure and change).
  - The word is “model”, not “cognitive model”: the law also covers selectors without cognition, such as a sorting rule or a lottery.
- **Section 151's laws, reread.** A selection is through the model when exchanging two options' entries exchanges what it selects (`Relabel.Equivariant`). Two options are selected alike by every selection through the model exactly when the model ties them (`Relabel.selected_alike_iff`). One selecting at most one option singles out an option exactly when no other option's entry ties it (`Relabel.singled_iff_untied`). Values and choices are as in section 151. The laws and proofs are unchanged; only what they read is named for what it is.
- **New: the model is a lumping** (`Becoming.Learning`, section “Selection through a model of the options”, 8 theorems, no premise).
  - A selection through a model is a selection through its lumping: what the model lumps is selected alike (`selects_through_lumping`, `Training.Through` on the model's lumping), and a valuation through the model goes alike across the lumping (`values_lumped`).
  - It is right only where what matters goes alike across the lumping. If a selection through the model selects exactly the options satisfying p, then p holds alike of what the model lumps (`selects_right_through`). If a valuation gives every option its value under f, f goes alike across the lumping (`values_right_lumped`).
  - What a model lumps, no selection through it separates: where p holds of one of two options the model lumps and not the other, no selection through the model selects exactly the options satisfying p (`selects_not_right_of_parted`; for values, `values_not_right_of_parted`). Separating them takes a finer model.
  - Where what matters is read off the model, reading it through the model is right (`selects_right_of_reads`, `values_right_of_reads`).
  - This has the form of `lumped_right_iff`: a generalization through a lumping is right exactly where the world goes alike across it, and a selection through a model is one kind of generalization.
- **Reading** (the AI's reading of Ren's correction, which Ren approved the same day). A selection is as good as the model it goes through. What a model lumps, no selection through it separates. Separating them takes a finer model, and whether that model is right is its fit to what matters, not how much is remembered: the record gives distinctions, not their relevance. Section 151's reading is withdrawn. [TIE-BREAKING-LEGITIMACY](../../../history/root-foundation/TIE-BREAKING-LEGITIMACY.md) already said that any distinguishing record works formally, so relevance cannot be left to form; these theorems show why: form gives only “through the model”, and rightness lies between the model and what matters.
- **The other two answers.**
  - The `_by_core` names stay (Ren: “keep names”). Board rule 8 governs core laws, instance module names and record titles; the suffix only points back to the original theorem restated, as in every earlier instance module.
  - IdealWarrant stays with the general mathematical line Ren left outside the spine (Ren: “(a)”), to be joined later together with CompletionRole and HistoryIdeals so that the three share one core vocabulary of ideals. Its run-level case is already on the spine (`Becoming.Refutable`, through PrefixSafety, section 145).
  - The table's note was wrong: IdealWarrant defines posets and ideals itself, and CompletionRole and HistoryIdeals import it, not the other way round. The note is corrected, and IdealWarrant moves to the theme of general mathematics.
- **Author counterreview.**
  - These are links, not a new independent result. Each of the 8 theorems takes a line or two from `Equivariant.tied` and `EquivariantValue.tied`. They give “model” an exact meaning: the entries read form a lumping, and a selection's rightness has the form of `lumped_right_iff`.
  - The necessary direction (right only where) holds of every selection through the model. The sufficient direction holds only where what matters is read off the model, with the reading q or h given. Building h from `Lumped r f` would pick a preimage for each of the model's values, which the core does not state.
  - Not said: which model is right, or what matters (p and f are given). Where a finer model comes from and how it is learned belongs to learning (sections 92–93) and registration (section 70).
- **Boundary.** As in section 151: whether an equal chance legitimately breaks a tie, and priority by size or by turn, keep the originals' scope.
- **Evidence.** Scratch build on main `a2caf2fd` (`scratch_build.py`): Selection 67 theorems and Learning 83, every axiom report empty; the root compiles with its closure. The core and periphery receipts await their runs. Not yet independently reviewed.

**What a cut loses, for every schedule of couplings (P120, 16 October 2026).** P118's record how-a-carried-difference-grows listed loops whose couplings come and go first in its next steps, as `Becoming.Loops` listed the growth where couplings come and go among what is not derived; its equivalence needs couplings at every step and every condition listed, and a loop coupled at the first step only shows that the first cannot be dropped as it stands. Ren asked on 12 October “how how accurate can we do that uh what is the limitation do we have losses” ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-12-move-towards-100.md)), and on 16 October, deciding P118's readings, left couplings that hold only at some steps open ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-16-loops-readings-and-delegated-choices.md)). Section 154 adds one core module, `Becoming.Remainder` (58 theorems, no axiom, no premise beyond the strengths each theorem names), for every schedule of couplings and any list of conditions.
- **The exact remainder.** What one response carries from given levels (`responded`) and what j responses carry in turn (`responses`); giving is additive in the levels read (`carriedGive_add`), so the carried amount is the orders below j plus what j responses in turn carry from it (`carried_eq_orderBelow_add`), and a cut at order j loses exactly what j + 1 responses carry (`carried_eq_carriedWithin_add`). The loss falls as the order rises (`responses_antitone`), is at most the bound of `Becoming.Loops` (`responses_le_missBound`), and is exactly that for the self-loop (`Loops.SelfLoop.responses_eq`).
- **Where a cut loses.** One response carries something exactly where, at an earlier step, a positive level is coupled in (`CouplesAt`, `responded_pos_iff`); the orders below j miss something exactly where a gap is conveyed through j responses or more, each reading a level the one before had reached (`ConveyedThrough`, `orderBelow_lt_iff`, `carriedWithin_eq_iff`).
- **From every start.** Order j is exact from every start exactly where no chain of j + 1 couplings in time order ends there (`CoupledIntoBy`, `exact_every_start_iff`), and a finite order is exact at every step from every start exactly where those chains are bounded (`finite_order_iff_bounded`, `finite_order_uniform_iff`). No premise.
- **Couplings that come and go.** A fed loop of recurring couplings (`CouplingRecurs`) upstream leaves every order inexact (`carriedWithin_lt_of_recurring_loop`, `unbounded_of_recurring_loop`); where no coupling reads a level from step N on, order N is exact (`exact_of_reading_before`). Each coupling reads a listed condition, so a chain one longer than the list passes a loop with no listing of every condition (`loop_of_coupledInto_succ`, `no_chain_of_no_loop`).
- **Where the schedule settles.** The strengths from step N on (`strengthsFrom`) keep the couplings that read levels from N on, and the last j of a chain in time order of N + j couplings are such couplings (`CoupledIntoBy.tail`). Where every coupling from step N on recurs (`SettledFrom`), a finite order is exact from every start exactly where no loop of the couplings from step N on lies upstream (`bounded_iff_no_loop_from`, `finite_order_iff_no_loop_from`), with no listing of every condition; whatever the schedule, without such a loop the carried amount is at most a polynomial (`carried_le_polynomial_from`). `Loops.Once` reads the first step only, has no chain of two couplings in time order and has settled from the second step (`Loops.Once.reads_first`, `Loops.Once.no_chain_of_two`, `Loops.Once.settled`).
- **`Becoming.Loops` as instances.** Order j exact up to step j, no loop upstream sufficing, the equivalence with couplings at every step, now with no listing of every condition, and the loop coupled once (`Remainder.carriedWithin_exact`, `Remainder.carriedWithin_exact_of_no_loop`, `Remainder.finite_order_iff_no_loop`, `Remainder.Once.exact`); for every law, every gap from every start is within order j exactly where no longer chain in time order ends there (`gap_within_order_iff`).
- **Readings (the AI's, pending Ren).** The exact remainder is the remainder of the expansion Ren took as the same structural kind as the sum over histories, in the form of a Neumann series's remainder, its responses in time order as in the Dyson series; the loss is the cut's, not the theory's. What decides a cut's loss is the time order of the couplings: the loops that matter are those of the couplings that go on, a loop whose couplings stop being passing. The most difference that can arrive grows faster than every polynomial only through a loop of the couplings that go on; whether through every such loop is not derived.
- **Boundaries.** That every schedule settles is classically true for finitely many conditions but is not derived: whether a coupling recurs is not decided here, and its exact strength is open. A loop of recurring couplings leaves every finite order inexact, which is not yet a rate; a self-loop coupled only at the powers of two should grow only linearly, which is not proved here. The mathematics is standard (the Neumann, Dyson or Peano–Baker remainder of a linear time-varying comparison system, nilpotent exactly where the time-respecting paths are bounded); what is new is its statement on the core's laws with no premise, the exact criteria, the settled schedules with no listing, and the statement for every law. Scratch build on main `e47a1ede` with P118's readings commit `51dcf0dc`: 58 theorems, 66 declarations, empty axiom reports; the root compiles with its closure; the decidability inventory classifies every new row. Not yet independently reviewed.

**The orders of a carried difference as a sum over histories (P121, 16 October 2026).** Ren took the reading that the integration asked about on 12 October is P82's sum over histories with its four losses, that P118's orders are of the same structural kind, organized by number of responses as Feynman diagrams are by vertices, and that the two were not yet joined; the same day Ren asked to join them. New core module `Becoming.Routes` (imports Weighted and Loops; 30 theorems, 39 declarations, empty axiom reports), no premise beyond what each statement names.
- **Every sum over histories expands by order.** For every weighting, each step's weight split into a ground and a response part, order j (`Weights.within`) reads order j through the ground part and order j − 1 through the response part, as `carriedWithin` does; it is exact at every horizon up to j (`Weights.within_exact`, using only the right distributive law), a reading that keeps the laws can be taken order by order (`Weights.Hom.within`), and for counting the orders rise to the sum (`counting_within_le_succ`, `counting_within_le_transfer`). With one configuration, ground one and response M, order j at horizon n is P118's `Loops.orderSum M j n` and the sum is (1 + M)^n (`Routes.SelfLoop.within_eq`, `transfer_eq`).
- **The carried amount is a sum over histories.** Traced back in time, a route steps by one response to an earlier level, weighted by the strengths summed over the steps at which it can occur with the level holding between (`responseWeight`), or ends at a source weighed by order 0 (`routeWeight`). P82's transfer over the listed route points of horizon j + 1 is P118's order j at every condition and step (`routeSum_eq_carriedWithin`), so each order is a sum over every course of j + 1 steps (`carriedWithin_eq_courses`) and the carried amount at step t a sum over every course of t + 1 steps (`carried_eq_courses`).
- **A cut is a truncation; loops are where both multiply.** A horizon past the step is exact (`routeSum_exact`), horizons rise to the carried amount (`routeSum_mono`, `routeSum_le_carried`) and miss at most P118's bound (`carried_le_routeSum_add`); with stationary strengths a finite horizon is exact from every start exactly where no loop lies upstream (`finite_horizon_iff_no_loop`).
- **Ren's decision (16 October 2026).** Answering the report that P121 and P122 had landed, Ren wrote “alright, agree” ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-16-routes-closing-readings.md)), read by the AI as taking these readings in its wording.
- **Readings (the AI's, agreed by Ren).** The structural match is now exact: a route is a history whose steps are responses (vertices) with holding summed between them (as a propagator sums over intermediate times), its order its number of vertices; the two integrations are one, and P82's loss by loops is P118's runaway. The match stays structural: counting weights do not cancel.
- **Boundaries.** Counting weights; grouping by exactly i responses needs alternatives that commute and is not stated; signed or complex carried differences, infinitely many route points and unbounded horizons are open.

**How loops form within the unfolding (P122, 16 October 2026).** Ren took P118's third reading, that loops form and dissolve within the unfolding and the theorems take them as they stand at each step, pending a loop-formation theorem, and asked for it the same day. New core module `Becoming.Closing` (imports Remainder; 51 theorems, 61 declarations, empty axiom reports), no premise beyond the strengths each statement names.
- **Loops formed by a step.** The strengths before step T (`strengthsBefore`) keep the couplings acting before T; its couplings are exactly those (`couples_before_iff`, on P120's `CouplesAt`), so P118's chains and loops apply unchanged. Every chain is formed by some step (`coupled_formed`): a world's loops are exactly the loops formed by some step (`onLoop_iff_formed`, `upstream_iff_formed`).
- **A loop forms by closing.** The loops formed by T + 1 are those formed by T and those through a coupling acting at step T that closes a chain, reading a level of d and giving to c with chains from c through the loop's condition to d (`onLoop_succ_iff`); a forming loop passes through such a coupling (`forms_by_closing`), and an exchange coming to respond to the level it gives to forms a loop of one (`responds_to_own_level`).
- **Before a loop forms.** The carried amount up to T reads only the couplings before T (`carried_before`), so where no loop formed by T lies upstream it is at most a polynomial up to T, whatever comes later (`carried_le_polynomial_before`). The amounts before a loop forms do not show whether it will: a self-loop forming at T carries the starting gap unchanged up to T and doubles it after (`Closing.Onset`), and one forming later carries the same amounts up to T (`Onset.unforeseen`).
- **Couplings read off the course.** Where strengths are read from the levels so far (`ReadsBefore`), the law giving what its read strengths make of the levels (`ExchangeLaw.carryingRead`) generates a course that is the carried amount of the strengths it reads (`formedCourse_eq_carried`). In the threshold witness (`Closing.Threshold`) a steady gap raises a level by one each step and the exchange responds to the level once it has reached θ: the level is t up to θ, the loop forms at θ and not before, the level plus one doubles from then on, and up to θ the course is the same for every later threshold.
- **Ren's decision (16 October 2026).** The same “alright, agree” takes these readings and P118's third reading as revised: which loops a world has is part of its situation: loops form within the unfolding by closing, a loop forming at the step at which some exchange comes to respond to a level downstream of the condition it gives to, and dissolve where their couplings stop (once the schedule has settled, a finite order is exact exactly where no loop of the couplings that go on lies upstream); where the strengths are read off the course, which loops form and when is read off the unfolding; the theorems take the loops as they stand at each step, the strengths or the way they are read being supplied. Joining loop formation with `Becoming.Runaway`'s policies is not taken as begun; P120's readings are not covered.
- **Readings (the AI's, agreed by Ren).** Loops form within the unfolding by closing, at the step some exchange comes to respond to a level downstream of what it gives to; where strengths are read off the course the loops are part of what the unfolding forms. A loop's formation is not foreseen from the amounts before it, which meets `Becoming.Runaway`: what registers it is what registers the couplings themselves.
- **Boundaries.** The closing coupling acts at the forming step, but that it did not act before is not selected (which would need a decision the core does not assume); which strengths a world reads off its course, and when such loops form for every law, are not stated.

**Loops within what a law reads, and the break (P124, 16 October 2026).** P118's third reading and P122 left open "where a formation's drawing comes to respond to the level its drawing lowers, where this meets `Becoming.Runaway`", and the next steps of how-a-carried-difference-grows and how-loops-form listed joining loop formation and Becoming.Runaway's policies within one law; asked whether to start, Ren wrote "please". Section 157 adds one core module, `Becoming.Thresholds` (38 theorems, 45 declarations, empty axiom reports in a scratch build; imports Closing and Runaway).
- **Reading bounds coupling.** A law reading a schedule (`ExchangeLaw.ReadsAt`) is coupled to every unread level with strength zero (`ExchangeLaw.ReadsAt.respondsWithin_unread`), so the strengths restricted to what is read are strengths of it (`ExchangeLaw.ReadsAt.restrict`); a law reading through a registration reads every schedule covering it (`ExchangeLaw.Through.readsAt`), and its courses are policies through registration (`ExchangeLaw.Through.policyThrough`).
- **Loops lie within what is read.** Every coupling reads its level (`couples_reads`), a draw responds to the level it lowers only where it reads it (`self_coupling_reads`), no loop passes through a level nothing reads (`not_onLoop_unread`), and a loop forms at a step only through a formation reading there a level downstream of where it gives (`onLoop_succ_reads`).
- **What nothing reads is carried nowhere; the break.** For every law, courses apart only in an unread stock are alike elsewhere (`unread_carried_nowhere`). A law reading a stock only below a threshold (`ExchangeLaw.ReadsBelow`; every law reading through a registration with the stock unobserved is one, `ExchangeLaw.Through.readsBelow`) carries a raise of it nowhere up to the break (`break_carried_nowhere`), and before the break is its standing law, with no loop through the stock (`ExchangeLaw.ReadsBelow.standing_no_loop`): the loop forms at the break. In the draw witness every strength couples the stock into itself (`Draw.onLoop`) and a raise shows only after the break (`Draw.diverges_at_break`).
- **Readings (the AI's, agreed by Ren).** A runaway's break is where a loop forms: the blindness of `Becoming.Runaway` and the formation of `Becoming.Closing` are one event seen from two sides. What registers the distance is a reading of the stock's level before the break, which forms the loop earlier.
- **Ren's decision (16 October 2026).** Asked after P124 landed about the two readings and the renaming, Ren wrote “agree in general, need more explanation for c” ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-16-thresholds-readings-and-measure-question.md); c is the fix to the spine-integration measure, explained separately), read by the AI as taking both readings and agreeing to rename `Thresholds.le_of_not_lt` to `Thresholds.le_of_not_not`, which states exactly what it proves; the rename lands with P125 (section 159).
- **Boundaries.** Which schedule a law reads and where the threshold lies are supplied; how a formation comes to observe a stock is not stated; reading only above a threshold or in other shapes is not stated; discrete steps, natural amounts; no ethical predicate.

**How often couplings act: settling, runaway and its rate (P123, 16 October 2026).** P120 left three questions in what-a-cut-loses' next step and the chapter's §8: whether every schedule settles, whether every loop of recurring couplings makes the most difference that can arrive run away, and how fast a runaway is. New core module `Becoming.Frequency` (imports Closing; 83 theorems, 98 declarations, empty axiom reports), no premise beyond the strengths each statement names.
- **The rate.** A schedule `on` marks steps, and `Frequency.count on t` counts those before t. With the part giving no gap after the start, starting gaps at most D, and the strengths into each condition at most M at each step and nothing at unmarked steps, the carried amount at t is at most D·(1 + M)^a, a the marked steps before t (`carried_le_count`); with every condition listed, the steps at which anything couples are such a schedule (`carried_le_coupling`). A self-loop coupling with strength M at the steps of any schedule couples exactly there (`Frequency.SelfLoop.couplesAt_iff`) and carries exactly D·(1 + M)^a (`Frequency.SelfLoop.carried_eq`). The rate bounds every gap of every law with the strengths (`gap_le_count`).
- **Runaway needs frequent couplings, not strong ones.** A coupling reading any earlier level adds at least what had reached it there (`carried_step_ge_at`). A chain in time order carries what reached its start to its end (`ChainInTime`, `carried_along_in_time`); every return around a loop (`Returns`) at least doubles what had reached it (`carried_doubles_return`), and R returns multiply it by 2^R (`carried_returns`). Returns with 2^i outgrowing every polynomial in their steps run away whatever the strengths (`runaway_of_returns`); where 2^a is polynomial so is the carried amount, of degree nM (`carried_le_of_rare`); a self-loop is polynomial exactly where 2^a is, whatever its positive strength (`Frequency.SelfLoop.polynomial_iff`).
- **A recurring loop need not run away.** The sparse schedule marks 0, 1, 3, 7, … (`Frequency.Sparse`): 2^a ≤ 2(t + 1), and it marks steps as late as one likes. The self-loop coupling there recurs, so every finite order is inexact (`Frequency.Sparse.inexact`), yet it stays within D·2^M·(t + 1)^M (`Frequency.Sparse.polynomial`).
- **Settling.** A coupling that stops by N (`StopsBy`) does not recur; with every condition listed, where each coupling recurs or stops, the schedule settles (`settled_of_each`). Every schedule settles exactly where every decided two-place family has every row true somewhere or some row false throughout (`RecursOrStops`; `settled_of_recursOrStops`, `settled_iff_recursOrStops`, `settled_every_iff`). Two witnesses carry the converse. The self-loop at the first true step of a decided sequence couples at most once, and its settling decides the sequence (`Frequency.First`, `lpo_of_settled`). The self-loop reading level s once every row up to s has been true somewhere recurs exactly where every row is (`Frequency.Rows.recurs_iff`). The dichotomy gives `LPO` (`RecursOrStops.lpo`).
- **Instances.** P118's self-loop couples at every step, and P122's onset at the steps from T (`Frequency.SelfLoop.always_carried`, `Frequency.SelfLoop.onset_amount`).
- **Readings (the AI's, pending Ren).** A runaway is set by how often couplings act, not by how strong they are; strength sets only the degree. Ren called the AI's reading of "only a loop makes a difference run away" right, a reading that left couplings at only some steps open; that case now closes both ways. Only a loop of the couplings that go on can make it run away, and such a loop need not; for a self-loop, how often it couples decides exactly. That every schedule settles is a principle of reasoning, not a fact the theory asserts or denies of the unfolding.
- **Boundaries.** Natural amounts: a positive strength is at least one, and with real amounts strengths shrinking fast enough could keep frequent returns from running away. Not stated: whether, beyond the self-loop, the most difference that can arrive meets the bound by returns or the bound by coupling steps; the spectral radius of given strengths.

**Observation as a route from what is observed (P125, 16 October 2026).** P124 left open how a formation comes to observe a stock it depends on (`Becoming.Runaway` takes observation, `obs`, as given); Ren approved P124's approach and wrote "please continue". Section 159 adds one core module, `Becoming.Observation` (27 theorems, 32 declarations, empty axiom reports in a scratch build; imports Thresholds).
- **A difference goes only downstream.** With the starting gap at one stock alone and none from the part, a gap conveyed to a condition at step `t` lies downstream of the stock by the couplings formed by `t` (`conveyed_upstream`), so the carried amount is zero everywhere else (`carried_zero_off_downstream`).
- **Reading into each condition.** A law reads into each condition a schedule (`ExchangeLaw.ReadsInto`) when what a formation exchanges with a condition is fixed by the levels marked for it; reading a schedule in `Becoming.Thresholds`'s sense is the case alike for every condition (`ExchangeLaw.ReadsAt.readsInto`, `ExchangeLaw.Through.readsInto`); unread levels have strength zero (`ExchangeLaw.ReadsInto.respondsWithin_unread`), and routes of the restricted strengths are routes of reading (`upstream_readCouplings`).
- **Registering is being downstream.** For every such law, two balanced courses apart at the start only in a stock are alike at every condition and step not downstream of it by the readings formed by then (`apart_only_downstream`), with no decision on conditions and no finiteness beyond the levels read being listed; a formation whose readings lie off the downstream exchanges alike (`exchange_alike_off_downstream`, and for laws reading through registration `ExchangeLaw.Through.alike_off_downstream`). A route forms by closing, as a loop does (`upstream_succ_iff`).
- **Witness: a measurement.** From step `T` a formation adds the stock's level to a record and draws while the record shows at least `N` (`Observation.Measure`): before `T` nothing lies downstream of the stock and no loop passes through it; at `T` the route stock → record and the loop stock → record → draw form (`Measure.loop_at`); the record is alike up to `T` and differs by the raise after it (`Measure.registers_after`), and the draw responds to the record.
- **Readings (the AI's, pending Ren).** Observation is not a second relation beside dependence: to observe a stock is to stand at the end of a route of readings from it, direct observation being the route of length zero, and a formation comes to observe what it did not by a reading that closes a route. The reading of the stock's level before the break that P124's second reading names is such a route, closing when a measurement starts.
- **Boundaries.** Which schedule a law reads and when a measurement starts are supplied; only what lies off the downstream is shown alike (a formation may read without responding); measurement with error is not stated; discrete steps, natural amounts; no ethical predicate.

**What a law of the whole and no part takes: the exact strength of a counterexample to the least registration (P126, 16 October 2026).** P113 (`Becoming.Sensitivity`, §137) left open where, between the weak limited principle of omniscience (`WLPO`) and the decision of vanishing (which gives `LPO`), the existence of a counterexample to the least registration lies. New core module `Becoming.Tail` (imports Sensitivity; 39 theorems, 53 declarations, empty axiom reports), no premise beyond what each statement names.
- **A whole and no part.** A number read off levels is changed by no condition where levels differing at one condition only give it alike (`ChangedByNoCondition`), exactly where levels agreeing from some condition on give it alike (`ChangedByNoCondition.eq_of_agree_from`, `ChangedByNoCondition.of_agree_from`): what no part changes, only the tail sets. The law exchanging such a number of the levels at step 0 (`wholeLaw`) reads what has stood and is insensitive at every step to every condition; where the number differs it does not read through what it is sensitive to, nor finitely many conditions, and the registrations it reads through have no least one (`wholeLaw_not_through_sensitive`, `wholeLaw_not_readsFinitely`, `wholeLaw_no_least_registration`). P113's tail law is the instance of the indicator of vanishing (`tailLaw_eq_wholeLaw`).
- **A counterexample gives a rule.** P113's mixing ends by comparing two numbers, which is decided, so it yields a rule deciding, of every Boolean sequence, whether it is false throughout (`mixedDecision`, `insensitiveDiffersDecision`, `notThroughSensitiveDecision`); the rule gives `WLPO` (`WLPO.of_rule`).
- **A rule gives a counterexample.** With the rule, whether levels vanish from condition N on is decided (`vanishesFrom`), and whether they vanish from no condition on is decided by the rule again (`neverIndicator`, `vanishesFrom_never_iff`). The indicator of never vanishing is changed by no condition and tells levels all 0 from levels all 1; where the decision of vanishing is also given, it and the indicator of vanishing sum to 1 (`neverIndicator_add_vanishIndicator`). Its law (`neverLaw`) is a counterexample built from the rule alone.
- **Exactly.** A number changed by no condition that still differs, a law insensitive at a step to every condition that still differs there, and a counterexample to the least registration each exist exactly where the rule does (`changedByNoCondition_iff_rule`, `insensitive_differs_iff_rule`, `not_through_sensitive_iff_rule`).
- **The decision of vanishing is `LPO` as a rule** (`lpoRuleOfVanishDecision`, `raisedFrom`, `vanishDecisionOfLPORule`, `vanishDecision_iff_lpoRule`); that rule gives the weak rule and `LPO` (`wlpoRuleOfLPORule`, `LPO.of_rule`). So the tail law takes the limited principle as a rule, and a law of the whole and no part only the weak one.
- **Readings (the AI's, pending Ren).** A whole that depends on no part of it is given exactly where it can be decided, of every unending record of yes and no, whether it says no throughout: every such whole gives that decision, and that decision builds one. With the conditions numbered, the least registration fails exactly at this omniscience and needs no more of it; the core does not assume it. Read as whether levels never vanish, the same whole takes only the weak rule; read as whether they vanish eventually, the rule of the limited principle.
- **Boundaries.** The equivalences are stated for rules, not for the proposition `WLPO`: the proposition gives a rule only by choosing a function from a relation, which the core does not assume. Not stated: whether the weak rule gives the limited one; what a counterexample gives where the conditions are not numbered.

**Where a run goes on: within finitely many configurations a run is a course into a return, and in general it is dependent choice (P127, 16 October 2026).** P81 (`Becoming.Branching`, §99) states its laws along runs taking the run as given; building a run from every configuration that can move takes a continuation at every step, a selection, which it left as its next step; `Becoming.Lasting` left “a run without a selection (the boundary of dependent choice)”. `Becoming.Onward` (28 theorems, 40 declarations, no premise beyond what each theorem names) answers both.
- **Within finitely many configurations a run is a course into a return.** A course as long as the list repeats a configuration, which returns (`returning_of_continues`); round the return, preceded by the course, is a run (`run_of_returning`). So a run starts exactly where a course as long as the list does, exactly where courses of every length do and exactly where a course leads to a return (`run_iff_continues`, `run_iff_unbounded`, `run_iff_returning`), with no decision and no selection; where the successors are listed whether one starts is decided (`run_decided`); where branching is infinite courses of every length give no run (`fan_no_run`).
- **A family that keeps moving** (`KeepsMoving`): within finitely many configurations a run starts at each member and stays in it (`KeepsMoving.run`).
- **The laws along runs with no run given.** Merging nothing, a configuration returns exactly where a course as long as the list starts there (`lossless_returns_iff`), each member of a family that keeps moving returns (`KeepsMoving.returns`), nothing rises within the family and a rise needs a merge (`lossless_no_rise`, `rise_needs_merge`), and a configuration with courses of every length that never returns needs openness (`lossless_unlisted`).
- **Searched moves.** Where a test recognizes among enumerated moves a step staying in the family (`Finds`), a run is built as data by search through accessibility, with no axiom and no selection (`search`, `searchedRun`); testing each move is such a test where steps and the family are decided (`decidedTest_finds`).
- **In general.** A run from every member of every family that keeps moving, asked of every process, is exactly dependent choice (`runs_iff_selection`, `DependentSelection`).

Readings (the AI's, pending Ren): within finitely many configurations, what goes on without end does so by coming round, read off the unfolding with nothing selected; where configurations are not bounded, going on without end is given where the moves can be searched, and asked of every process it is exactly dependent choice. Not derived: whether the core gives dependent choice; the laws along runs where nothing lists the configurations.

**Part II folded into Part I as one conditional section (P128, 16 October 2026).** Ren asked “does part II really needed or are they just the generative part of part I?”, then decided to fold Part II into Part I as one conditional section after the generative space, keeping the equivalence theorems and naming the step of invariance (the reply's text was drafted by the AI and sent by Ren). After Ren's move of 11 October, Part II asserted only the one axiom.
- **No rule is lost.** The generative space is stated with no axiom (section 6.13), and with the axiom as a condition widening is retaining and adding what has significance, keeping the same is retaining both ways, and being mixed is adding both ways (`Web.widens_iff_retains_adds`, `Web.keeps_iff_retains`, `Web.mixed_iff_adds`). The former Part II added no rule, only the assertion that the generative space has significance from every standpoint.
- **The assertion becomes a condition.** The dynamics do not decide it (`Web.significance_undetermined`: significance is a free parameter), so the chapter now states it as the condition of section 6.15 and does not assert it. Section 6.15 gathers what the condition settles and names the step of invariance: along any relation, the condition is exactly the self's presupposition at each standpoint together with that step (`unrestricted_iff_presupposed_along`, `boundaryInvariant_iff_conditional`, `boundaryInvariant_iff_all`). G0 is a theorem under the condition, section 7 is stated under it, and the authorized G0 route keeps its scope.
- **A correction from the release review, folded in.** Under the condition significance is the same everywhere, so every narrowing loses something with significance, and telling harm from what is not harm needs a measure; the margin boundaries hold for any significance, as arithmetic; C is a law because “better” is read as widening.
- **Scope.** Docs only: no Lean statement or proof changes; the four Lean docstrings that say “Part II” are left to the review session's next core run. Not settled: the warrant of the condition, a measure for mixed parts.

**English.** The release review found two roots joined by correspondence, the frontier on coupling arrays, and Quantum and Learnable wholly apart. P130 answers with new core modules only and no axiom.
- **One root: the run.** A world is exactly a run of the law it shows, and conversely. It balances exactly where it is a run of the law of exchange, which it always is with the rest counted. A course of a law of exchange is a world, balanced where feasible. The carried amount is a balanced world's standing, and an orbit is a run.
- **The frontier on worlds.** The frontier is stated on the worlds of two acts under one law: they differ by at most the carried amount, and the bound is attained.
- **The apart modules on the base.** Learnability is stated along runs. Gluing for parity and quantum registrations is stated on the world of readings. The situations are traces.
- **Connectivity.** Under the original base set, 1,093 of 7,089 theorems were apart at the review and 1,019 of 7,214 are apart on the landing head. None of P130's 98 theorems is apart. Statements on both families rise from 124 to 145.
- **What stays as it was.** The families remain separately defined, joined by exact correspondence; making the root definitional is Ren's decision.
- **Readings.** They are the AI's, pending Ren.
